title: NEXT F Accessibility Control Registry
description: Machine-readable accessibility standards for customer websites, Customer CMS, NEXT F Admin and the Contract Portal.

categories.label: Forms & Validation
categories.description: Labels, instructions, help and error association.

categories.label: Keyboard & Focus
categories.description: Keyboard operation, visible focus and focus management.

categories.label: Interactive Components
categories.description: Dialogs, drawers, menus, tables and complex controls.

categories.label: Authoring & Editors
categories.description: Accessible editing, rich text and content-authoring metadata.

categories.label: Visual Presentation
categories.description: Contrast, reflow, touch targets and non-color-only meaning.

categories.label: Status & Feedback
categories.description: Live regions, loading, errors and status messages.

categories.label: Navigation & Discovery
categories.description: Navigation, skip links, filters and command palette.

categories.label: Management Interfaces
categories.description: Customer CMS, Admin and operational interfaces.

controls.name: NEXT F Admin accessibility
controls.requirement: NEXT F Admin tables, context selectors, diagnostics, dialogs and privileged actions must satisfy applicable accessibility controls and must not communicate risk/status by color alone.
controls.rationale: Internal administration must remain operable and understandable for keyboard and assistive-technology users.

controls.name: Use ARIA with restraint
controls.requirement: ARIA must supplement native semantics only when necessary and must not contradict native roles, states or properties.
controls.rationale: Incorrect ARIA can make otherwise accessible native controls unusable.

controls.name: Accessible authentication flows
controls.requirement: Sign-in, verification, recovery and recent-authentication flows must expose labels, instructions, errors, status and keyboard operation without inaccessible challenge assumptions.
controls.rationale: Authentication accessibility failures can completely block account access.

controls.name: Author accessibility metadata
controls.requirement: Schema/UI metadata should expose accessibility-relevant authoring requirements such as alt text, accessible labels, help/error association, caption/transcript references and heading constraints where applicable.
controls.rationale: Schema-driven editors need machine-readable cues to present accessible authoring requirements consistently.

controls.name: Provide data alternatives for charts
controls.requirement: Charts and visual data representations must provide an accessible textual/table alternative or equivalent programmatic data representation.
controls.rationale: Visual position and color cannot be the only path to underlying data.

controls.name: Accessible checkout flow
controls.requirement: Checkout must preserve labels, validation, error recovery, keyboard operation, progress/status context and review/confirmation access without pointer-only interaction.
controls.rationale: Checkout is a critical transaction flow where accessibility failures can block purchase completion.

controls.name: Customer CMS accessibility
controls.requirement: Customer CMS resource lists, editors, actions, dialogs and validation must satisfy the applicable accessibility controls and preserve keyboard alternatives for authoring workflows.
controls.rationale: Customers must be able to manage content without accessibility regressions in the management interface.

controls.name: Accessible code and raw-data views
controls.requirement: Code/raw-data viewers must preserve selectable text, readable overflow behavior and keyboard-accessible copy actions without requiring syntax color to understand content.
controls.rationale: Technical source views are primary content in the Contract Portal.

controls.name: Do not rely on color alone
controls.requirement: Status, validation, risk and selection states must communicate meaning with text, iconography, shape or semantics in addition to color.
controls.rationale: Color alone excludes users with color-vision differences and can disappear in forced/high-contrast modes.

controls.name: Meet contrast requirements
controls.requirement: Text, interactive states and essential non-text UI indicators must provide sufficient contrast against adjacent backgrounds.
controls.rationale: Low contrast can make content and controls unreadable.

controls.name: Accessible copy actions
controls.requirement: Copy actions must be semantic buttons with an accessible name and must expose success/failure feedback without relying only on visual change.
controls.rationale: Copy is a frequent action in technical interfaces.

controls.name: Accessible dialogs
controls.requirement: Dialogs must expose dialog semantics, an accessible name, keyboard containment while modal, predictable close behavior and focus restoration.
controls.rationale: Modal content requires explicit semantics and focus management.

controls.name: Provide alternatives to drag and drop
controls.requirement: Any drag-and-drop operation must have a keyboard-accessible non-drag alternative that performs the same action.
controls.rationale: Dragging can be inaccessible to keyboard and some motor-input users.

controls.name: Accessible drawers
controls.requirement: Navigation and action drawers must expose their state, support keyboard closing, and manage focus without trapping users behind the drawer.
controls.rationale: Drawers are modal-like interactions on smaller screens and need equivalent keyboard behavior.

controls.name: Accessible filters
controls.requirement: Search and filter controls must have labels, keyboard operation, deterministic state, clear/reset behavior and a discoverable result count.
controls.rationale: Filters are core navigation tools in management and technical interfaces.

controls.name: Visible keyboard focus
controls.requirement: Keyboard focus must always have a clearly visible indicator on interactive controls.
controls.rationale: Visible focus is required for users to understand current keyboard position.

controls.name: Manage focus across UI transitions
controls.requirement: Dialogs, drawers and route-level transitions must move, contain, restore or announce focus intentionally according to the interaction pattern.
controls.rationale: Unmanaged focus can leave keyboard and screen-reader users disoriented.

controls.name: Associate labels with inputs
controls.requirement: Every user-editable form control must have an explicitly associated visible or programmatic label.
controls.rationale: Labels provide the accessible name and persistent context for input controls.

controls.name: Associate descriptions and help
controls.requirement: Help text, constraints and descriptions must be programmatically associated with the field when they affect successful input.
controls.rationale: Visible helper text that is not associated may be missed by assistive technology.

controls.name: Associate validation errors
controls.requirement: Validation errors must identify the affected field programmatically and provide actionable text.
controls.rationale: Users need to locate and understand validation failures without relying on color or position alone.

controls.name: Communicate required input
controls.requirement: Required state and input requirements must be conveyed in text or semantics, not only by visual styling.
controls.rationale: Required-field meaning must remain available independent of color and visual layout.

controls.name: Logical heading structure
controls.requirement: Pages and authored content must use a logical heading hierarchy without using heading level only for visual styling.
controls.rationale: Heading structure supports orientation and efficient navigation.

controls.name: Constrain authored heading levels
controls.requirement: Structured content blocks that expose headings must support a valid content outline and must not use heading levels only for typography.
controls.rationale: Schema-driven content can otherwise generate invalid heading hierarchy even when the editor shell is accessible.

controls.name: Handle icon semantics correctly
controls.requirement: Decorative icons must be hidden from assistive technology; meaningful icon-only controls must receive an accessible name.
controls.rationale: Repeated decorative icon names can create noise while unlabeled icon buttons hide control purpose.

controls.name: Alternative text for meaningful images
controls.requirement: Meaningful images must have appropriate alternative text; decorative images must be intentionally hidden from assistive technology.
controls.rationale: Image purpose must remain available when visual content cannot be perceived.

controls.name: Full keyboard operation
controls.requirement: All functionality must be operable from a keyboard without requiring pointer-specific interaction.
controls.rationale: Keyboard access is fundamental for many assistive-technology and motor-impaired users.

controls.name: Expose page landmarks
controls.requirement: Primary page regions such as navigation and main content must use semantic landmarks or equivalent labeled regions.
controls.rationale: Landmarks help assistive-technology users navigate major regions.

controls.name: Use live regions deliberately
controls.requirement: Live regions must use an appropriate politeness level, avoid noisy repeated announcements and contain concise status text.
controls.rationale: Overly broad or frequent live regions can make dynamic interfaces unusable.

controls.name: Accessible loading and error states
controls.requirement: Loading, empty and error states must provide text that identifies the state and the next available action where applicable.
controls.rationale: Users must not depend on spinners, color or visual placement to understand system state.

controls.name: Captions for synchronized media
controls.requirement: Prerecorded video with meaningful spoken content must support captions when the content requires them.
controls.rationale: Captions provide equivalent access to spoken audio.

controls.name: Transcripts where applicable
controls.requirement: Audio-first or information-dense media must provide a text transcript or equivalent alternative where applicable.
controls.rationale: Transcripts support users who cannot access audio and improve review/searchability.

controls.name: Accessible menus
controls.requirement: Menus and menu-like controls must use an interaction model consistent with their semantic role and provide keyboard equivalents for every action.
controls.rationale: Custom menus can create keyboard traps or inconsistent navigation if roles and keys disagree.

controls.name: Preserve accessibility on responsive layouts
controls.requirement: Responsive transformations must preserve reading order, control names, keyboard access, focus visibility and complete functionality on narrow viewports.
controls.rationale: Mobile/tablet layout changes must not create a separate inaccessible interaction model.

controls.name: Respect reduced motion
controls.requirement: Non-essential animation and transitions must respect the user reduced-motion preference and must not be required to understand content.
controls.rationale: Motion can cause discomfort or prevent successful interaction for some users.

controls.name: Accessible names for controls
controls.requirement: Every interactive control must expose a stable accessible name that communicates its purpose.
controls.rationale: Unnamed controls are difficult or impossible to operate with assistive technology.

controls.name: Accessible navigation state
controls.requirement: Navigation must expose meaningful link text, current-route state and an operable small-screen alternative without hiding functionality from keyboard users.
controls.rationale: Navigation is a repeated critical path across the portal and management interfaces.

controls.name: Accessible command palette
controls.requirement: Command palettes must support keyboard opening, result navigation, Escape closing, focus containment/restoration and announced result state.
controls.rationale: Keyboard-first discovery must remain predictable to keyboard and screen-reader users.

controls.name: Support zoom and reflow
controls.requirement: Content and primary workflows must remain usable under browser zoom and narrow reflow without requiring two-dimensional scrolling except where intrinsically necessary.
controls.rationale: Zoom and reflow are essential for low-vision access and smaller displays.

controls.name: Accessible rich-text editing
controls.requirement: Rich-text editors must expose toolbar controls, editing context and formatting actions to keyboard and assistive technology, with a non-pointer path for all supported operations.
controls.rationale: Authoring tools must not make content editing dependent on pointer input.

controls.name: Use semantic HTML
controls.requirement: Use native semantic HTML elements for structure and controls before adding ARIA or custom interaction roles.
controls.rationale: Native semantics provide robust names, roles and behaviors across browsers and assistive technologies.

controls.name: Provide skip navigation
controls.requirement: Repeated navigation must provide a keyboard-accessible mechanism to move directly to main content.
controls.rationale: Skip links reduce repetitive keyboard navigation.

controls.name: Announce important status changes
controls.requirement: Important asynchronous status changes must be exposed to assistive technology without unexpectedly moving focus.
controls.rationale: Users need feedback when operations complete, fail or update asynchronously.

controls.name: Accessible data tables
controls.requirement: Data tables must identify headers and relationships programmatically; responsive transformations must preserve data context.
controls.rationale: Table structure is needed to associate cells with their meaning.

controls.name: Provide usable touch targets
controls.requirement: Frequently used interactive targets must be large and separated enough for reliable touch operation.
controls.rationale: Small adjacent targets increase accidental activation.
